chapters.title: Between Damocles and Hydra
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter installs the missing map: fragile is harmed by volatility, robust resists it, and antifragile gains from bounded stress.
chapters.coreMove: Sort a system by its response to volatility before deciding whether to shield it, test it, or leave it alone.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating antifragile as a fancy synonym for resilient toughness.

chapters.title: Overcompensation and Overreaction Everywhere
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter treats rebound, redundancy, and suppression backfire as cases where stress produces extra capacity or attention.
chapters.coreMove: Recognize when spare capacity and rebound are adaptive reserves rather than waste.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming every overreaction is wise or every redundant layer is inefficiency.

chapters.title: The Cat and the Washing Machine
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter separates living adaptive systems from mechanical systems that mostly accumulate wear under use.
chapters.coreMove: Decide whether a system needs protection from wear or bounded challenge that carries useful information.
chapters.commonMisread: Managing bodies, skills, and machines with one universal smoothness model.

chapters.title: What Kills Me Makes Others Stronger
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter develops dose and hormesis: low stress can strengthen while higher stress can destroy.
chapters.coreMove: Read the dose curve before deciding whether a stressor teaches, trains, or simply damages.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning hormesis into either overprotection or macho more-is-better advice.

chapters.title: The Souk and the Office Building
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter contrasts decentralized local trial-and-error with centralized order that can hide concentrated fragility.
chapters.coreMove: Prefer error-correcting local feedback when central neatness would spread mistakes silently.
chapters.commonMisread: Reading the chapter as a simple anti-institution or anti-planning rant.

chapters.title: Tell Them I Love (Some) Randomness
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter argues for selective randomness where downside is limited and upside remains open.
chapters.coreMove: Invite variation only where losses are clipped and learning or upside can compound.
chapters.commonMisread: Confusing bounded randomness with liking chaos everywhere.

chapters.title: Naive Intervention
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter critiques interventions that remove visible pain while increasing hidden fragility and blocking feedback.
chapters.coreMove: Pause before relieving a signal and ask what adaptive feedback the discomfort may be carrying.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating all help, treatment, or intervention as automatically harmful.

chapters.title: Prediction as a Child of Modernity
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter criticizes forecast prestige in opaque domains and shifts attention to payoff, exposure, and humility.
chapters.coreMove: Replace prediction pride with exposure mapping when the domain is too opaque for clean forecasts.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking the lesson is to stop learning or stop estimating altogether.

chapters.title: Fat Tony and the Fragilistas
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter pits payoff-sensitive practical judgment against polished abstraction that ignores exposure.
chapters.coreMove: Test an elegant explanation by asking what concrete bet it would accept and who bears the loss.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing Fat Tony to anti-learning attitude or street-smart performance.

chapters.title: Seneca's Upside and Downside
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter frames uncertainty through asymmetry, survival, and clipping downside rather than average-case comfort.
chapters.coreMove: Judge an uncertain choice by its downside floor and upside opening, not by the average story.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning Seneca into generic stoic lifestyle advice.

chapters.title: Never Marry the Rock Star
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter argues for the barbell: protect against ruin while keeping selective exposure to large upside.
chapters.coreMove: Build a barbell by separating protected essentials from small, optional bets with open upside.
chapters.commonMisread: Reading the rock-star warning as dating advice or timid moderation.

chapters.title: Thales' Sweet Grapes
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter uses optionality to show how favorable outcomes can be captured without precise prediction.
chapters.coreMove: Seek rights without obligations when uncertainty is high and upside can be captured cheaply.
chapters.commonMisread: Calling optionality indecision or passive waiting.

chapters.title: Lecturing Birds on How to Fly
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter argues that practice, tinkering, and contact with reality often precede clean theory in complex domains.
chapters.coreMove: Let reality-tested tinkering produce knowledge before demanding a complete theory.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating theory as useless or practitioners as automatically wise.

chapters.title: When Two Things Are Not the 'Same Thing'
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter warns that surface similarity and neat labels can hide decisive structural differences.
chapters.coreMove: Break an apparent equivalence by comparing response structure, downside, and payoff under stress.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the lesson into abstract wordplay about labels.

chapters.title: History Written by the Losers
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter argues that retrospective stories often miss what practitioners actually built and why it worked.
chapters.coreMove: Distrust neat after-the-fact explanations and recover the practitioner logic that produced the result.
chapters.commonMisread: Making this a broad anti-history complaint.

chapters.title: A Lesson in Disorder
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter treats bounded mess, trial, and self-discovery as informative in uncertain life.
chapters.coreMove: Use small disorder to discover fit where tidy planning would only preserve assumptions.
chapters.commonMisread: Celebrating chaos as inherently creative.

chapters.title: Fat Tony Debates Socrates
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter closes the optionality section by sharpening payoff-grounded practical judgment against abstract interrogation.
chapters.coreMove: Resolve a reasoning dispute by returning to exposure, consequence, and the payoff of being wrong.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating Socrates as the villain or practical judgment as anti-thinking.

chapters.title: On the Difference Between a Large Stone and a Thousand Pebbles
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter opens nonlinearity by showing that concentrated and distributed impacts are not equivalent.
chapters.coreMove: Check whether many small hits and one large hit have different consequences before aggregating them.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating nonlinearity as abstract math rather than a practical damage rule.

chapters.title: The Philosopher's Stone and Its Inverse
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter focuses on transformation, inversion, and interventions under hidden response structures.
chapters.coreMove: Invert the desired transformation and ask what hidden response could turn a fix into its opposite.
chapters.commonMisread: Getting lost in mystical metaphor instead of practical reversal.

chapters.title: Time and Fragility
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter begins Via Negativa by treating time as a revealer of hidden fragility and survival information.
chapters.coreMove: Use survival across time as evidence, while still asking what exposures the thing has actually faced.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning time into generic patience or nostalgia.

chapters.title: Medicine, Convexity, and Opacity
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter applies asymmetry and opacity to intervention-heavy domains, especially medicine-like systems.
chapters.coreMove: Intervene more readily when upside is convex and downside limited, and hesitate when hidden harm dominates.
chapters.commonMisread: Reading the chapter as crude anti-medicine or anti-treatment rhetoric.

chapters.title: To Live Long, but Not Too Long
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter applies Via Negativa to longevity through subtraction, restraint, and avoiding avoidable harm.
chapters.coreMove: Improve survival odds first by removing fragility-amplifying inputs rather than adding heroic fixes.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the lesson into generic health hacks or immortality chasing.

chapters.title: Skin in the Game: Antifragility and Optionality at the Expense of Others
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter moves into ethics: people should not keep optional upside while exporting downside onto others.
chapters.coreMove: Reject decisions where the actor keeps upside and transfers the tail risk to someone else.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating skin in the game as a macho slogan about taking risks.

chapters.title: Fitting Ethics to a Profession
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter applies skin in the game to professional roles, where abstract codes are weak without real exposure.
chapters.coreMove: Fit an ethical rule to the profession by tracing its real downside channels and incentives.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing ethics to written codes, slogans, or reputation management.

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.sourcePressure: The conclusion synthesizes fragility, antifragility, time, optionality, subtraction, and skin in the game through asymmetry and consequence.
chapters.coreMove: Classify what should be protected, what can be stressed, and where asymmetry or exported downside changes the decision.
chapters.commonMisread: Ending with chaos worship or a universal formula for every system.
